title: Ordinary and derived positive root charts of the actual integral-reduced line
statement: Fix the finite-coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], the actual integral-reduced signed coefficient lines [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data] and their normalized signed products [def-pur-finite-signed-twist-products]. Use the specified zero and first-root charts [def-pur-finite-first-root-chart]. Lift the specified derived first-root chart uniquely through the fully faithful degree-zero single functor to an ordinary coefficient sheaf chart. The ordinary positive chart family is uniquely characterized by sending each ordered local basis power of its first-root generator to the coefficient-one section, with coefficient one at zero. The signed products identify these charts with the ordered positive tensor-power recursion. Take their singles and the native single/unit comparison to obtain the positive derived charts.

source.place: Proof Step 2: compatibility with the invertible twist by associativity of derived tensor, all signed twists and shifts; returned proof Step 1 (twist part)

proof.text: Lift the prescribed first derived chart through the fully faithful degree-zero single functor, after composing with the inverse single/unit comparison. Mathlib Functor.preimageIso gives the lift; mapIso_injective gives uniqueness. This is the existing proved singleUnitChart_existsUnique helper.

Construct the entire ordinary positive family by finiteTensorOrdinaryChartRecursion from the specified first ordinary chart. Its coefficient-unit zero chart and signed-product successor formula are explicit data. Apply the recursion normalization theorem to obtain FiniteTensorSheafChartsNormalized.

For any other normalized family, fix a degree d. Its chart and the recursive chart both send every compatible frame vector to the same coefficient-one section. Their values agree by transitivity of equality. Apply finiteTensorPositiveChart_frame_ext to the hom maps, then Iso.ext and function extensionality. This proves uniqueness and hence the required existsUnique assertion.
